first.rationale: The simultaneous declines in onboarding completion and activation suggest a funnel constraint that may suppress qualified revenue across self-serve accounts. Simplifying onboarding directly addresses completion and time-to-value without immediately conceding margin. Verify memory_86 for downstream revenue and retention durability, and memory_73 to compare whether targeted pricing produced sustainable cohort economics under competitive pressure. Guard against removing steps that predict successful long-term adoption.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified prior test improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current funnel declines. Promotional pricing is rejected despite competitive pressure because its 18% qualified-revenue lift was accompanied by a 12% retention decline and failure through first renewal. Measure qualified activation, retention, and revenue—not completion alone—and retain safeguards against removing steps essential to durable adoption.
